title: Compact compatibility sprint - scribe
content:
Sprint: compact-model compatibility (week 2026-06-21) - freeform notes and next steps

Context:
- Goal: validate 4-bit/8-bit compact model variants (two config families) for onboarding into Redwood serving runtime without regressions in latency or generation quality for common customer prompts. Focus this week: KV prefetch interactions, attention kernel stability, and lightweight eval suite run against three prompt baskets.
- Running on test infra: g4dn-proto-cluster and a local nvlink box (dev-quant03).

High-level summary / quick wins:
- KV prefetch with 4-bit quant (symmetric per-tensor) works on basic autoreg test harness; transient drop in perplexity at sequence boundary resolved by padding heuristic (see experiment 03 below).
- Microbatch path (batch size 4, max latency 120ms) showed ~12% CPU-side serialization overhead — we have an easy optimization (serialize fewer small tensors) to try next sprint.
- Preliminary eval: BLEU-like proxy / coherence score across our short dialog basket shows 1.8% delta vs fp16 baseline for Q4 variant (within acceptance for most routes). Q3 variant (aggressive clipping) shows visible tone collapse on long-form prompts.

Detailed experiment notes:
- EXP-01: baseline fp16 (control) on dev-quant03
  - prompts: 50 short-dialog, 20 code-complete, 30 long-form
  - avg token latency: 9.8ms
  - RL proxy coherence: 0.92
  - notes: clean run, used as reference for artifacts

- EXP-02: Q4 symmetric (per-tensor) without kv-prefetch
  - avg token latency: 6.1ms (raw kernel time down)
  - coherence: 0.90 (-0.02 vs baseline)
  - issues: occasional spike at segment boundary with longer prompts (see EXP-03)

- EXP-03: Q4 + KV prefetch enabled + padding heuristic (pad to next multiple of 16 tokens before prefetch)
  - avg token latency: 6.4ms (prefetch overhead ~0.3ms but reduced end-to-end jitter)
  - coherence: 0.91 (recovered)
  - observation: padding heuristic avoids partial-kv fallback path that previously forced fp16 path for last chunk.
  - TODO: formalize heuristic as a runtime config (flags: prefetch_pad_multiple=16) and add unit tests (PR link in linked_artifacts).

- EXP-04: Q3 aggressive clipping (size-opt) on microbatch path (batch=4)
  - avg token latency: 5.9ms
  - coherence: 0.86 (not acceptable for production chat routes)
  - failure modes: hallucination rate increased in long-form prompts; logits scaling unstable when sequence length > 1024.
  - follow-up: stop further rollout of Q3; investigate rescaling strategies in quant kernel (candidate: per-head scale rescaling).

Operational notes / infra hiccups:
- dev-quant03 crashed midday due to OOM from an unrelated test runner; snapshot available (logs in jira ML-2187). Re-ran EXP-02 on g4dn-proto-cluster with consistent results.
- Telemetry: token-level traces missing for ~12% of runs due to buffer flush race; tracking in github:inference/telemetry issue#122. Needs small change in tracing middleware to atomically commit buffer before async flush.

Evals and metrics to surface for Product/Console:
- Per-route accepted delta thresholds: define and track coherence delta (proxy metric) and hallucination-rate delta. Proposed thresholds: coherence delta <= 0.03; hallucination delta <= 0.02 for chat routes; lower tolerance for knowledge-grounded completions.
- Add rollout gating: block canary if hallucination delta > 0.015 on any prompt basket sample.

Open research questions / hypotheses:
- H1: padding to 16-token boundaries reduces kv cache incompatibilities across mixed-precision kernels; can we make this automatic without token-level waste? Explore cache alignment vs compact encoding tradeoff.
- H2: per-head rescaling during quantized matmul stabilizes logits for aggressive clipping variants — need small-scale experiment (slot for next sprint).
- H3: microbatch serialization cost is dominated by small-tensor mallocs in CPU-side preparation; changing allocator or reusing staging buffers should drop serialization by ~8-15%.

Meeting notes (weekly sync 2026-06-22) - attendees: Dana, Rohit, Lina, Omar, Priya (SRE)
- Lina: suggested adding a prompt basket specifically for enterprise docs conversion (longer context + citations) — agreed, Lina to assemble 20 prompts by EOD Friday.
- Omar: flagged telemetry buffer race; will open PR to make flush atomic and add fuzz test.
- Rohit: recommends gating Q4 rollout behind a canary route that excludes long-form customer-facing completions; will draft rollout plan and canary config.
- Priya (SRE): asked for exact memory footprint delta numbers for Q4 vs fp16 to update Dedicated capacity planning; Dana to provide numbers by Mon.

Action items (owner - due):
- Lina Chen - assemble enterprise prompt basket (20) - 2026-06-25
- Omar Alvarez - PR for telemetry atomic flush + fuzz test - 2026-06-24 (draft expected)
- Dana Kim - memory footprint table (per-model-variant) + CSV for capacity team - 2026-06-28
- Rohit Mehra - canary rollout plan + route config (block rules) - 2026-06-25
- Research owner (TBD) - design per-head rescale experiment and small harness - 2026-07-02

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Q3-like variants slip into shared model catalog causing customer regressions. Mitigation: enforce model-variant metadata tags (stability: alpha/beta/stable) and automatic blocking of alpha on default routes.
- Risk: telemetry gaps mask regression signals. Mitigation: immediate fix + backfill for missing traces on critical runs.

Notes to self / rough checklist for next sprint:
- push prefetch_pad_multiple into runtime flags and add unit/integration tests
- add enterprise prompt basket to evals runner and re-run EXP-03+EXP-04 only on that set to gather longer-context behavior
- schedule microbench for allocator reuse (dev-quant03) and measure serialization delta
- start a short doc: "compact-variant-rollout-guidelines" for Solutions/CS referencing gating thresholds and expected cost/latency tradeoffs

Quick links referenced in sync:
- jira: ML-2187 (OOM / re-run logs)
- github:inference/compact-kernel PR#678 (kernel tweaks for symmetric quant)
- confluence:APPLIED-ML/compat-checklist-2026

Misc scribbles:
- possible nice-to-have: automatic kv-pad detection in compiler that emits prefetch-pad hints inline in model metadata. Could reduce our per-route flag surface.
- thought: add a small synthetic that stresses attention edge-case (masking + variable chunk sizes) to CI, run weekly on dedicated CI cluster.

End of notes.

-- Dana
